rules.rule: Check for urgent throat symptom conditions
rules.problem: check_for omits the BP < 90/60 measurements (systolic and diastolic) that the urgent rule and anaphylaxis rule depend on, so the clinician is never prompted for BP. Allergen exposures lack the past-few-hours window.

rules.rule: Assess throat symptoms not needing urgent attention
rules.problem: Triggered only by sore throat, so a patient with only difficult/painful swallowing is never asked about white patches, although the candida rule fires without sore throat. Also missing: "If food/liquid gets stuck with swallowing, refer" (no food-sticking finding or referral rule), and tender neck lymph nodes from the viral box.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from throat symptoms with sudden face/tongue swelling
rules.problem: Structure (sudden face/tongue swelling AND any of the list) is faithful, but drug/food exposure without the footnote's past-few-hours window makes the second arm almost always true, so sudden face/tongue swelling alone effectively yields possible anaphylaxis. "Check for" is not literally "consider".

rules.rule: Diagnose probable oesophageal candida from painful or difficult swallowing
Diagnose possible diphtheria from throat/nose pseudomembrane
rules.problem: Faithful: sore throat AND pseudomembrane in throat or nose, "Consider" maps to possible; fever is correctly optional. Pseudomembrane is a morphologic-abnormality concept (no finding concept exists).

Logic matches the page: no pseudomembrane, swollen tonsils AND (exudate OR no cough OR no runny nose). Bacterial tonsillitis is_a Infective pharyngitis, an acceptable concept for tonsillopharyngitis (Pharyngotonsillitis has no bacterial child).

The No branch is negated correctly (no swollen tonsils OR (no exudate AND cough AND runny nose)). The extra gate on red throat or swollen tonsils comes from the viral box description and is reasonable; tender neck lymph nodes are not used.

rules.rule: Urgent: throat symptoms with danger signs
rules.problem: Urgent matches "Give urgent attention ... Refer urgently". All four bullets are present with OR, and the anaphylaxis bullet is correctly nested as swelling AND any-of. Minor: the allergen timing is dropped, and "red swelling blocking airway" is approximated as Pharyngeal swelling AND URT obstruction.

summary: Most consequential: allergen exposure (drug/food/insect) drops footnote 1's "within the past few hours" window, so in the anaphylaxis and urgent rules ordinary food exposure plus sudden face/tongue swelling satisfies the any-of arm. The non-urgent assessment task triggers only on sore throat, so isolated dysphagia never prompts the oesophageal-candida check, and "food/liquid gets stuck, refer" is not encoded. Face and tongue swelling should use the precoordinated Facial swelling / Tongue swelling concepts; the core diagnostic branching (diphtheria, bacterial vs viral) is faithful.
